svg.title: Planning & development
svg.desc: Decode the request: Identify form, audience, purpose and context. Use a supplied title. Write: “I want this reader to ... because ...”. Do not change the task to fit a memorised answer. Select a clear position: For an argument, decide your main claim. For advice, decide the useful action; for review, your judgement. Consider the reader’s needs and worries. An editor can publish views, but cannot personally change a school rule. Different points: For clubs: learning a skill, meeting people, fitting attendance around commitments. Three versions of “clubs are fun” are repetition. Each paragraph should add something new. Develop one point: Point → detail → explanation → reader. Use this as a thinking route, not a fixed formula. Example: small coding task → visible success → unfamiliar skills feel learnable. Explain the connection. Order paragraph jobs: Persuade: concern → benefits → obstacle and response → action. Advise: preparation → first action → likely difficulty → next step. Discuss: weigh views → reasoned judgement. Plan quickly: Use brief paragraph notes and one useful example for each key point. No compulsory paragraph count. Check that the ending follows from the plan. Keep time to draft and edit both tasks.
